newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World Infra loan raised to $600 mln.
newsitem.headline: New World Infra loan raised to $600 mln.

text.p: New World Infrastructure Ltd has increased the size of its five-year revolving credit/term loan facility to US$600 million from US$500 million, the deal's coordinating arrangers said on Tuesday.
The issue amount was increased following oversubsription in the underwriting stage, coordinating arrangers HSBC Investment Bank Asia and Goldman Sachs (Asia) said.
They said the issue represents the first fundraising exercise of the borrower since it was listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in October 1995.
The issue was launched into general syndication today.
New World Infrastructure is a subsidiary of New World Development Co Ltd.

Its principal business activities are to develop, own, operate and/or manage toll roads, expressways, tunnels and bridges, power stations, container terminals, cargo handling and storage facilities, and cement manufacturing in Hong Kong and China.

Proceeds of the loan facility will be used for general working capital of New World Infrastructure and its group companies. The deal pays an interest margin of 85 basis points and has a five-year tenor with bullet repayment at maturity.
In addition to the coordination arrangers, 11 banks have joined the facility as arrangers and lead managers.

They are Bank of China Hong Kong branch, China Construction Bank Hong Kong branch, Credit Lyonnais, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Hong Kong branch, Hang Seng Bank, Peregrine Fixed Income, Societe Generale Asia, United Overseas Bank, Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale, Banque Indosuez and Banque Nationale de Paris Hong Kong branch.
